items.title: NEW — Organize Imports OVER-PRUNES a named leaf whose module the file still needs for its `impl`s: `import pkg::a::b;` with `b` unused fades as "unused import" and the action DELETES the statement, but `a.vl`'s `impl Style { fun select_off(self) .. }` arrived through that import (impls travel with ANY import reaching the module, not only a whole-module one), so the next analysis is "Style has no method 'select_off'" — the organizer broke a green build (reproduced 2026-09-12: s1c → s5). `import_leaf_is_used` rule (2) — "a whole-module import brings every impl in that module's file" — keeps a MODULE leaf on the file's provenance test, and a NAMED leaf never reaches that test. Fix: when every named leaf of a statement is unused but the file resolves something DECLARED in the module's file (rule (2)'s own test, applied to the statement's module), REWRITE the statement to `import pkg::a;` instead of deleting it; the fade stays on `b` (it is unused) and the action's edit is the rewrite
items.discussion: the owner's report (2026-09-12) — kolt's extension impls on std types (`select_off`, the view helpers) are the exhibit; the owner's alternative is a LANGUAGE change (impls arrive only with an explicit `import a;`), which is breaking for every file that reaches an impl through a named import today — recommended: the rewrite, no language change; the alternative is recorded as a ruling if the owner wants the language to say it
items.body:
**Mechanism.** In `Document::organize_imports` (the `keep` predicate threaded into `formatter::organize_run`/`prune_import_branch`, formatter.rs ~1454), a statement whose every leaf is unused is today dropped by `prune_import_branch` returning `None`. New step before the drop: resolve the statement's module (the path minus its leaves; for a brace set, the common prefix), and ask rule (2)'s question of it — does `reference_index.occurrences_in(entry)` (excluding occurrences written inside import statements) contain a definition whose `declaration_source` is that module's file? If yes, the statement becomes `import <module>;` (rendered through the same canonical printer, sorted into place). If no, drop as today.

**Fade.** `unused_import_spans` keeps fading `b` — it IS unused — and the hover/fade text for that leaf can say "unused; the module's impls are in use, Organize Imports rewrites this to `import pkg::a;`" so the mark and the fix agree (E114's contract).

**Pins.** (1) `import pkg::a::b;` + `const { style().select_off() }` → rewrite to `import pkg::a;` and the rewritten file analyses clean; (2) `import pkg::a::{ b, c };` with `c` used → `{ c }` as today (the rewrite only fires when nothing survives); (3) `import pkg::a::b;` with neither `b` nor any impl used → deleted as today; (4) a module import + impl use → kept (the existing kolt.local 004 pin); (5) the fmt/organize agreement pin (`organize_imports_renders_a_split_run_the_way_fmt_does`) extended with a rewrite case. Docs: the editor page's Organize Imports row gains one sentence.

items.title: NEW — Organize Imports OVER-KEEPS a whole-module import: `import pkg::a;` beside `import pkg::a::b;` with only `b` used is kept (no fade, no action; reproduced 2026-09-12: s2), because `import_leaf_is_used` rule (2) keeps a MODULE leaf when the file resolves ANYTHING declared in the module's file — and `b`'s uses are declared there, though the named leaf, not the module import, provides them. Count for the module leaf only what the module import ALONE provides: occurrences whose definition is NOT bound by another import leaf of this file (methods of the module's impls, and `a::x` qualified paths — which reference the module leaf itself and are already rule (1)'s)
items.discussion: the owner's report (2026-09-12): 'Organize Imports sometimes keeps module imports even when there are no usages of it including impls'; the kolt exhibit is any file that grew an `import pkg::x;` for an impl and later imported the names it needed by leaf
items.body:
**Mechanism.** Rule (2) in `Document::import_leaf_is_used` (document.rs, the `DefinitionKind::Module` arm) tests `declaration_source(occurrence.definition) == home`. Refine: build the set of definitions bound by this file's OTHER import leaves (`type_references` entries at each leaf span, aliases included — the map `unused_import_spans` already walks), and skip an occurrence whose definition is in that set. What remains is what only the module import brings: method occurrences resolved to impls declared in `home`, and anything the file reaches by `a::` qualification (those occurrences reference the module leaf and rule (1) keeps it). A module import whose remaining set is empty is unused: fades and prunes.

**Edge.** A definition reached BOTH through a named leaf and through the module (`a::b()` and `b()` in one file): the qualified use references the module leaf directly (rule (1)), so the module import survives — correct.

**Pins.** (1) `import pkg::a;` + `import pkg::a::b;`, `b()` used → the module import fades and prunes, `b`'s stays; (2) `import pkg::a;` + `const { style().select_off() }` (impl use) → kept (kolt.local 004's pin, unchanged); (3) `import pkg::a;` + `a::b()` → kept; (4) `import pkg::a;` alone, nothing used → pruned (today's behaviour, s3). E168 and E169 are one lane — they edit the same predicate and the same pin file.
